clue.text: Bird following fashion? No way!

indicators.note: the bird comes after the word for fashion, so its letters are written second

parts.note: to fashion something is to forge it
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A question about a bird copying the latest trend, met with a flat refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are blunt spoken refusals telling someone their request will never happen.

clue.text: Gift of Gladstone or one of his opponents

parts.note: Gladstone led the Liberals, so a single opponent of his would be a Tory, with 'one' giving A

explanation.surface: A remark on the Victorian prime minister's talent, or on one of his political rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Gladstone, the Liberal prime minister, was famed for his speeches; his rivals were the Conservatives, nicknamed Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladstone was renowned for eloquent public speaking, the art of the formal speech.

clue.text: Try and upset poetess with pace of Nazi advance

parts.note: to have a go is to make a try

indicators.note: upset means the letters of poetess are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to disturb a female poet using the stiff marching gait of German troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The stiff-legged marching step was the parade style of Nazi German soldiers.

clue.text: Bone one's broken somewhat upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the column upside down, so the letters read bottom to top
the numeral one has broken into the phrase for somewhat, sitting inside it

parts.note: somewhat means a bit
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone's bone is fractured and they are a little distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' puts I inside A BIT to give AIBIT, and 'upset' turns that upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The shinbone of the lower leg is a bone.

clue.text: Scots began their sports with this

definitions.text: Scots began their sports with this

parts.words: Scots began their sports with this
parts.note: 'began' hides a pun on a felled tree trunk, so the Highland Games event is a log-hurling contest

explanation.surface: A claim about how Highland Games first started.
explanation.walkthrough: The caber is a long pole; read 'began' as a pun, sport opens with a heave of a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurling a long wooden pole end over end is a signature event of Scottish Highland Games.

clue.text: One beset by Fury, an apparition

indicators.note: one is surrounded by the word for fury, so it sits inside it

parts.note: fury means wrath
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone surrounded by an avenging Fury, a ghostly figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost or spectral vision of a person is an apparition.

clue.text: Movie genre you and I back

parts.note: you and I together are we
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Two people reverse together towards a film style.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboy films set on the American frontier form a film genre.

clue.text: Old European fish

definitions.meaning: a member of a Germanic people who settled in England in the fifth century
to fish with a rod and line

explanation.definitionFit: The early tribe that gave England its name is one sense; to cast with rod and line is the other.

clue.text: One bidding good health to bloom

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: Someone raising a glass to a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who proposes a toast wishes the company good health.

clue.text: One's leader behind mob, perhaps

indicators.note: the leading letter comes after the headwear, so it is written second

parts.note: a mob cap is a type of old-fashioned bonnet

indicators.note: the leader of the word one is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A gang boss standing behind his criminal mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mob' looks like the gang, but a mob cap is a frilly bonnet, so 'mob, perhaps' gives CAP. The whole clue also describes a Mafia boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A capo is a Mafia chief, the head of a criminal mob.

clue.text: Eye with alarm perhaps ring denoting engagement

parts.note: busy is British slang for a detective, a private eye
an alarm is an example of a signal

explanation.surface: A watcher with an alarm, perhaps announcing an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engagement' and 'ring' suggest a wedding, but the ring is a telephone tone telling a caller the line is engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: The tone heard when a phone line is engaged tells the caller the line is in use.

clue.text: Artist gets an advance to use for trade

parts.note: Claude Monet was a French Impressionist painter
a rise is an advance in pay or price

explanation.surface: A painter receives a cash advance.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something serve as currency or bring it into commercial exchange.

clue.text: Art collector rejecting good artist

indicators.note: the collector's name throws out the letter for good

parts.note: J. Paul Getty was an oil magnate and famous art collector

explanation.surface: A collector turning down a fine painter.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was a nineteenth-century English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was an English painter known for nudes.

clue.text: Japanese city it's capital's moved to

indicators.note: the pair of letters spelling to are shifted to another place in the capital's name

parts.note: Tokyo is the capital of Japan

explanation.surface: A Japanese city that the capital has been relocated to.
explanation.walkthrough: TO moves from the front of TOKYO to the end, making KYOTO, itself a former capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyoto is a historic city in Japan, the old imperial capital.

clue.text: Battle with drink among a royal entourage

indicators.note: the drink goes among the letters of the royal retinue, inside them

parts.note: a monarch's attendants form the court
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Fighting over drinks amid a king's attendants.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V defeated the French at Agincourt in 1415, a famous battle.

clue.text: Aid to oarsman Dark Blues set off

definitions.text: Aid to oarsman Dark Blues set off

parts.words: Aid to oarsman Dark Blues set off
parts.note: rowing crews such as Oxford's Dark Blues use a bracket that projects off the side of the boat to carry the rowlock

explanation.surface: Equipment helping the Oxford crew as they set off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dark Blues are the Oxford crew in the Boat Race; the rowlock bracket is set off from the hull.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting bracket bearing a rowlock helps a rower get more leverage on the oar.

clue.text: It can be illuminating to strike pledge

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
to plight one's troth is to pledge it

explanation.surface: A remark that hitting a promise can be enlightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from a lamp brightens a room, so it is illuminating.

clue.text: Resilient old pop star

definitions.meaning: the frontman of the 1980s band whose stage name was ...

explanation.definitionFit: Unbending firmness is one sense; the other is the stage name of an 1980s new-wave singer.

clue.text: I will swing for unkind act

parts.note: I will is contracted to I'll
to swing round is to turn

explanation.surface: A threat to hang for some cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing someone a bad deed is an unkind act, the opposite of a good deed.

clue.text: Holy man and a politician die

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A saint and an MP perish together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'die' is the noun: a tool that presses a pattern into metal or paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A die is a stamping tool used to impress a design, as on coins.

clue.text: Germ from fleece in rodents

indicators.note: the word for fleece goes in the rodents, inside their letters

parts.note: mice are rodents
to fleece someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: A bug picked up from wool among mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like wool but is the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is a microscopic organism that can cause disease.

clue.text: Service using Bible in New York

indicators.note: the Bible's letters go in the city's abbreviation, inside it

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A church service held in New York with scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The navy is one of the armed services, alongside army and air force.

clue.text: Hick follows pair with fifty

parts.note: a yoke is a pair of oxen harnessed together
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin trailing behind a couple and fifty others.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country dweller, a rustic.

clue.text: What's used to put together Scotch kilt?

definitions.text: What's used to put together Scotch kilt?

indicators.note: put together signals the letters of Scotch kilt assembled in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of sewing makes a Highland kilt.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a sewing-machine stitch that could join a kilt, while 'put together' also rearranges SCOTCH KILT.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine stitch interlocking two threads is used to sew fabric seams.

clue.text: Burns up what some types have

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from the bottom upward

parts.note: fires burn, and burns as a verb means fires

explanation.surface: The poet Burns and what certain people possess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' suggests the poet; 'types' are printing typefaces.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing a letter in certain typefaces.

clue.text: Epidural, perhaps, not a current issue

definitions.meaning: an anaesthetic injection into the spine numbs the lower body, so it is something that numbs the back
an old edition of a magazine or newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: A spinal anaesthetic deadens sensation in the lower body; separately, an old edition of a periodical is no longer current.

clue.text: One's crazy to continue

definitions.meaning: a silly or foolish person, a clown
to carry on or keep going

explanation.definitionFit: A buffoon or clown is one sense; carrying on with something is the other.

clue.text: Hot temperature advancing in English Channel region

indicators.note: the letter for temperature moves forward to an earlier place in the word

parts.note: the Solent is the strait off the English Channel between the Isle of Wight and Hampshire

explanation.surface: Rising temperatures in an English coastal waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' is slang for stolen goods; 'advancing' moves T forward in SOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolen goods are called hot because they are recently taken and risky to handle.

clue.text: Match official having made mistake submitted

parts.note: a ref is a referee
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A referee who made a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that has been passed on for decision has been submitted or sent on.
